translations.translatedText: # Friday 12.10.2018 (radio)
Master's studies have not become shorter. Kela-tärpit won the Clearest Speaker of the Year award. Emergency centres need more call handlers. The autumn school holiday starts in warm weather.
## University degrees take time
![A girl reads a entrance exam book.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9953229)
Open image viewer
Master's studies take about 6 years. Photo: Kati Latva-Teikari / Yle
Students today spend almost as much time completing a master's degree as they did 10 years ago. Master's studies take about 6 years in Finland.
The Finnish government's goal is that students complete their degrees faster. Universities say that the goal is hard to reach, because universities get less money from the state than before.

A master's degree is a higher university degree. A lower university degree, that is a bachelor's degree, goes faster for students nowadays than before. Nowadays a bachelor's degree takes a little under 4 years. A few years ago a bachelor's degree took about 5 years.
## Kela-tärpit is the Clearest Speaker of the Year
![Two women. One has a carpet beater in her hand and the other a certificate of honour.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10454386)
Open image viewer
Kela-tärpit won the Clearest Speaker of the Year award. Satu Kontiainen and Jenni Viinikka from Kela received the award. Photo: Pälvi Tammi / Yle
The Clearest Speaker of the Year award has been given out. The winner of the award is Kela-tärpit. The award was given out on Thursday, when Clear Language Day was celebrated.
There were 10 award candidates. An expert panel chose the 3 best of them. The winner was chosen by Petri Jääskeläinen, the Parliamentary Ombudsman.
The competition winner, Kela-tärpit, or Kela's tips, offers information about benefits on social media.
Kela-tärpit are on Kela's website and also at elamassa.fi. Kela-tärpit can also be listened to.
**Clearest Speaker of the Year 2018**
## Emergency centres lack call handlers

![Emergency centre call handler Tuuli Torssonen and shift supervisor Artturi Jortikka stand by their work at the Kerava emergency centre, but recently it has become more demanding because of a shortage of staff.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10442453)
Open image viewer
Call handler Tuuli Torssonen works at the Kerava emergency centre. Photo: Ulla Malminen / Yle

There are too few emergency centre call handlers in Finland. A call handler answers emergency calls. They assess what kind of help the caller needs. A call handler can, for example, send an ambulance to the scene.
Call handler Tuuli Torssonen works at the Kerava emergency centre. She hopes for more colleagues, because there is a lot of work.
There are 6 emergency centres in Finland. They need 35 new employees right away.
Emergency centre call handlers are trained at the Emergency Services College in Kuopio. The number of training places has been raised a little, but the emergency centres think it is still not enough.
## The weekend is warm
![Three-day temperature forecast](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10453609)
Open image viewer
Photo: Yle Weather
Next week the autumn school holiday is in a large part of Finland. The autumn holiday starts in warm weather.
On Saturday the temperature in the south is about 16 degrees, and on Sunday it is still a little warmer. On Sunday the sun may also shine in the south.
In the north it is colder. In Lapland the temperature over the weekend is between 5 and 10 degrees.
